deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the close of Part I of Gauss's Latin treatise on the arithmetic-geometric mean (AGM), 'De origine proprietatibusque generalibus numerorum mediorum arithmetico-geometricorum', c. 1800. The previous page established the following.
(i) (1/pi) Int_0^pi dphi / sqrt(1 - x^2 cos^2 phi) = y, where 1/y = M(1+x, 1-x) = M(1, sqrt(1-x^2)). Here M is the AGM.
(ii) The general theorem. Let W = alpha / sqrt(beta - gamma cos^2 phi) be expanded as P + 2Q cos 2phi + 2R cos 4phi + ... . Let v, v' be the extreme values of W. Then 1/P = M(1/v, 1/v'). For gamma > 0 the extremes are alpha/sqrt(beta-gamma) and alpha/sqrt(beta). The case gamma < 0 follows from phi -> 90deg - phi.
(iii) The claim that the same holds for alpha / sqrt(beta + gamma cos phi), with 1/P = M(sqrt(beta-gamma)/alpha, sqrt(beta+gamma)/alpha).

This page justifies (iii). Put phi = 2psi. Then cos phi = 2cos^2 psi - 1 [identity supplied by me], so beta + gamma cos phi = (beta - gamma) + 2gamma cos^2 psi. The function therefore takes the form alpha / sqrt(beta' - gamma' cos^2 psi) with beta' = beta - gamma and gamma' = -2gamma. This is exactly the form already treated.

Why the constant term carries over [my elaboration]:
- Its cosine series in 2psi, 4psi, ... is the series in phi, 2phi, ..., so the constant terms coincide.
- The extreme values are unchanged: alpha/sqrt(beta-gamma) and alpha/sqrt(beta+gamma).
- Hence 1/P = M(sqrt(beta-gamma)/alpha, sqrt(beta+gamma)/alpha).
In modern form: (1/pi) Int_0^pi dphi / sqrt(beta + gamma cos phi) = 1 / M(sqrt(beta+gamma), sqrt(beta-gamma)), for |gamma| < beta.

Footnote *). Suppose several expressions alpha / sqrt(beta + gamma cos phi) have the same extreme values. Then their constant terms must be equal, even if all other coefficients differ greatly. This is immediate, since P depends only on the extremes.

Closing remarks (no mathematics):
- A more general proof 'from more genuine principles' will follow later.
- Methods equally expeditious will be given for the remaining coefficients Q, R, S, ... .
- For readers who value truths only by their applications: the rapid evaluation of P, Q, R, S, ... is useful in physical astronomy, i.e. the theory of planetary perturbations.
The perturbation link is concrete [my illustration]. Take 1/sqrt(1 - 2a cos phi + a^2), so beta = 1 + a^2 and gamma = -2a. The constant term is then 1/M(1+a, 1-a) = 1/M(1, sqrt(1-a^2)). This is the leading Laplace coefficient (1/2) b_{1/2}^{(0)}(a).
errors: No mathematical errors. The reduction phi = 2psi and the identification of the extreme values are correct.
Implicit condition: |gamma| < beta (and alpha > 0) is needed for real square roots and a positive AGM. Gauss leaves this unstated.
Strictly, the sign of gamma only swaps which extreme is the maximum. Since M is symmetric, the formula holds for either sign; Gauss's gamma<0 remark on the previous page covers this.

results.what: Constant term of the Fourier cosine expansion of alpha/sqrt(beta + gamma cos phi): 1/P = M(sqrt(beta-gamma)/alpha, sqrt(beta+gamma)/alpha), via the substitution phi = 2psi reducing it to the cos^2 form
results.modern_name: AGM evaluation of the complete elliptic integral of the first kind, (1/pi) Int_0^pi dphi/sqrt(beta+gamma cos phi) = 1/M(sqrt(beta+gamma), sqrt(beta-gamma))
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (diary entry of 30 May 1799; this treatise, published posthumously in Werke III, 1866); related transformations by Lagrange and Legendre

results.what: Expressions with equal extreme values have equal constant terms (P depends only on max and min of W)
results.modern_name: Corollary of the AGM formula for the mean value

results.what: Remark that rapid AGM-type evaluation of the cosine coefficients P, Q, R, S serves planetary perturbation theory
results.modern_name: AGM computation of Laplace coefficients b_s^(k)(a), cf. Gauss's 'Determinatio attractionis' (1818)

deep.surprise_reason: This page belongs to Gauss's AGM treatise, printed in Werke III (Schering, 1866). The theorem and its extension to beta + gamma cos phi are well known as Gauss's. The page itself only performs a trivial substitution and adds programmatic remarks.

transcription_corrections: Page number '14' (top centre, inked) is the incorrect original pagination; the pencil/red '15.' at top right is the correct folio number.
The struck word after the first line ('Ceterum', replaced by 'Denique') is correctly read; the second struck word before 'earum pretium' is illegible and may be 'omnino' rather than 'omnia'.
'praecedd.' in the footnote is an abbreviation of 'praecedentibus'.
Otherwise the machine transcription matches the image; the formula alpha/sqrt(beta-gamma+2gamma cos psi^2) is read correctly.
